concept_html:
A unit test should not call a survey API, read a production table or depend on today's date. Lesson B2-L1 pushed side effects to the edges. Three tools handle what is left at those edges.

Pass the dependency in. A function that takes get or now as a parameter needs no tricks to test. The test passes a small fake:

class FakeResponse:
    status_code = 200

    def json(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        return {"respondents": 812}


assert wave_count("W14", get=lambda url, timeout: FakeResponse()) == 812

monkeypatch, a built-in fixture, changes something for one test and undoes it afterwards. monkeypatch.setenv("SURVEY_API_TOKEN", "test-token") sets an environment variable. monkeypatch.delenv("SURVEY_API_TOKEN", raising=False) removes it. monkeypatch.setattr(module, "name", value) replaces an attribute.

unittest.mock from the standard library builds stand-ins that record how they were called:

  • Mock(return_value=x) returns x on every call.
  • Mock(side_effect=[a, ConnectionError("down")]) returns a, then raises on the next call.
  • fake.assert_called_once_with(url, timeout=30) checks the arguments.
  • fake.call_count counts calls, including calls that raised.

patch("module.name") swaps a name for the length of a with block. Patch the name where the code looks it up. If reports.py does from requests import get, patch reports.get. Patching requests.get leaves reports.get pointing at the real function, and the test makes a real call.

Use mocks sparingly. A mock checks how your code talks to the outside world, not whether its result is right. Mock the boundary, such as HTTP, the clock or a database, and test the logic with real objects. Never mock pandas.

lines: from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any
import pytest
API = "https://survey.example/api/waves"
def wave_count(wave_id: str, get: Callable[..., Any]) -> int:
response = get(f"{API}/{wave_id}", timeout=30)
if response.status_code != 200:
raise RuntimeError(f"wave API returned {response.status_code}")
return int(response.json()["respondents"])
class FakeResponse:
def __init__(self, status_code: int, payload: dict[str, int]) -> None:
self.status_code = status_code
self._payload = payload
def json(self) -> dict[str, int]:
return self._payload
def test_wave_count_reads_respondents() -> None:
calls = []
def fake_get(url: str, timeout: int) -> FakeResponse:
calls.append((url, timeout))
return FakeResponse(200, {"respondents": 812})
assert wave_count("W14", fake_get) == 812
assert calls == [(f"{API}/W14", 30)]
def test_wave_count_raises_on_error_status() -> None:
with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="503"):
wave_count("W14", lambda url, timeout: FakeResponse(503, {}))

exercises.solution:
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

API = "https://survey.example/api/waves"


def wave_count(wave_id: str, get: Callable[..., Any]) -> int:
    """Number of respondents in one wave, from the survey API.

    Args:
        wave_id: Wave to look up.
        get: HTTP GET function, such as requests.get.

    Returns:
        The respondent count.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the API does not answer with status 200.
    """
    response = get(f"{API}/{wave_id}", timeout=30)
    if response.status_code != 200:
        raise RuntimeError(f"wave API returned {response.status_code}")
    return int(response.json()["respondents"])

title: Isolate I/O with fakes, monkeypatch and mocks
why_html: A test of a weekly loader patched requests.get, but the loader imported get by name. Every CI run quietly called the supplier's live API with a test token. The supplier rate-limited the account during a delivery week, and the real nightly load failed. Patching loader.get instead, or passing get in as a parameter, would have kept the tests offline.
